# EFC (express-file-cluster)

> An opinionated backend framework on Express: files in src/api become routes, clustering uses every CPU core, src/tasks holds background jobs (BullMQ or pg-boss), and defineModel / defineTable give typed models on MongoDB and PostgreSQL. Started with one ignite() call.

Install: `npx create-efc-app my-api`. Import paths: `express-file-cluster`, `express-file-cluster/auth`, `express-file-cluster/tasks`, `express-file-cluster/testing` — no others exist.

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://efc.prashantadhikari7.com.np/docs.html): quick start, project structure, configuration, routing, handlers, middleware, errors, clustering, tasks, auth, RBAC, database, mailer, API dashboard, generated portals, CLI, environment variables
- [Full reference on GitHub](https://github.com/pr4shxnt/efc.js/tree/main/docs)
- [MCP server](https://www.npmjs.com/package/express-file-cluster-mcp): `npx -y express-file-cluster-mcp` serves these docs to coding agents

## Project

- [Source](https://github.com/pr4shxnt/efc.js)
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/express-file-cluster)

## 0.11.0

OpenAPI: `ignite({ openapi: true })` serves `/openapi.json`; `generateOpenAPI()` also supports offline generation. Route validators need Standard JSON Schema or an explicit adapter.
WebSockets: export `WS` from a route file; middleware/auth run before the upgrade. Origin checks, payload caps, heartbeat and graceful draining are built in. Auth is handshake-only and broadcasts are worker-local.
